desk_read: Short covering was the session's dominant theme, lifting WTI by +2.77% and gold by +1.51% on shrinking open interest, the clearest signal that bearish positions are being unwound rather than fresh bulls stepping in. WTI's move looks fragile: volume came in at only 0.9x its 20-day average against an -18.1k contract drop in total open interest, so the rally has thin sponsorship. Copper told the opposite story — price fell -1.56% while open interest rose +4.4k contracts, a new-shorts read that makes it the session's most crowded directional bet. The Nasdaq stood out as the lone equity laggard, shedding -2.7% of total open interest on long liquidation even as the S&P edged higher, a divergence worth watching.
